text:
sarah_support: Customer (MapleHealth) hit a 413 from /v1/rerank and is blocked. They send a long user query + ~1,200 passages. Error body: `{ "error": "input size exceeded" }` — no guidance to fix. Can someone confirm limits and recommended worker-side guidance?

miguel_eng: Can you paste the exact request body (trim secrets) and the raw response? 413 means NGINX/edge or our API returning RequestEntityTooLarge. If it's the latter we should include limit details.

sarah_support: Pasting redacted curl + response below:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Long clinical summary: ... (7k chars)", "docs": [{"id":"p1","text":"..."}, ..., {"id":"p1200","text":"..."}] }'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large`
Body: `{ "error": "input size exceeded" }`

sarah_support: Customer says they used to send ~1,200 passages, each ~400 chars. They need to rerank all of them server-side (can't pre-filter easily).

miguel_eng: Repro steps I did locally with a similar payload: our request layer rejects payloads > ~1.5MB and we then return 413 with that minimal message. The cause is the combination of query+docs hitting the edge limit and our API lacking a helpful hint.

miguel_eng: Short-term suggestions to give customer: 1) chunk docs into batches (e.g., 200 at a time) and merge scores client-side; 2) pre-filter candidates with embeddings endpoint (cheap) then call rerank on top-K; 3) shorten query/passage fields or send excerpts. Will propose these to MapleHealth as workarounds.

ashley_pm: From product side, we should (a) update the error body to include which limit was hit (payload_bytes or docs_count) and the allowed limits, and (b) add a KB article with recommended patterns (batching, embeddings prefilter, passage trimming).

miguel_eng: I'll add an Engine bug to return a structured 413 like `{ "error": "input_size_exceeded", "reason": "payload_bytes", "allowed_max_bytes": "1536000", "hint": "try batching docs or prefiltering with embeddings" }` — relatively small change in the API layer. Also will add a short HTTP header `X-Allowed-Request-Bytes` as redundancy for proxies.

sarah_support: Nice. Can you also call out limits for docs count and per-doc chars so we can pass them to the customer?

miguel_eng: Current implicit practical limits (what I've measured): docs_count safe <= 500 in one call, total payload <= ~1.5MB, per-doc text ideally < 2k chars to avoid big blowups. Not hard limits we enforce per-field yet, hence the confusing message. We'll add explicit per-field caps in the KB.

ashley_pm: I'll own the KB write-up and wording. Suggest making the message prescriptive: e.g., "Payload too large — reduce docs per request (<=500), or use embeddings prefiltering. See KB: <support.redwood.ai/rerank-limits>". Also add a migration snippet showing how to chunk + merge scores.

miguel_eng: Implementation plan: patch API layer this sprint to return structured 413 and header, plus add a small validation that returns a 400 with `docs_count_exceeded` when docs array > 1,000 to give faster feedback (non-breaking). I'll post the PR link here when ready.

ci-bot: deploy status: no active deploys for /v1/rerank.

sarah_support: Great — can we get ETA so I can update MapleHealth CS?

miguel_eng: ETA: PR by EOD Tue this week, rollout to staging Wed, prod late next week if no regressions. I'll ping when staging is up with test curl examples.

ashley_pm: I'll draft the KB and a short email template for CS to send (including the temporary workarounds). Would like a short, explanatory sentence in the error body rather than a cryptic code.

sarah_support: Thanks team. I'll send the workaround steps to MapleHealth now and mark this escalated. Please @miguel_eng when staging is ready so we can repro with customer sample. :thumbsup:

miguel_eng: ack. I'll include a sample chunking script and an embeddings-filter example for KB.

sarah_support: Closing loop for now — I'll reopen if customer still blocked after workarounds or after the API patch.
